## Dataset

```{r}
#| label: load-dataset
#| message: false

events <- read_csv(
  "data/event_participants.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

donations <- read_csv(
  "data/contributions.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

event_contacts <- events |>
  distinct(`Contact ID`)

donor_contacts <- donations |>
  distinct(`Contact ID`)

overlapping_contacts <- event_contacts |>
  inner_join(donor_contacts, by = "Contact ID")
```

This project will use two datasets exported from Watershed Management Group's (WMG) CiviCRM database. WMG uses CiviCRM
to track community event participation and financial
contributions.

The first dataset contains `r nrow(events)` event participation
records across `r ncol(events)` variables, representing
`r nrow(event_contacts)` unique contacts. These records include
information such as event titles, event dates, participant
statuses, and participant identifiers.

The second dataset contains `r nrow(donations)` financial
contribution records across `r ncol(donations)` variables,
representing `r nrow(donor_contacts)` unique contacts.
Variables include contribution dates, donation amounts,
contribution statuses, and contribution identifiers.

Both datasets contain a shared Contact ID variable, allowing
event participation records to be connected with financial
contributions. An initial comparison identified
`r nrow(overlapping_contacts)` contacts appearing in both
datasets, representing approximately
`r round(nrow(overlapping_contacts) / nrow(event_contacts) * 100, 2)`%
of all event contacts.

I selected these datasets because I am currently working at WMG, helping 
to increase community engagement and build a stronger relationship with
the community. I am interested in understanding whether community events
are associated with future financial contributions and continued donor
engagement. I will be presenting this analysis to leadership at WMG to
help upper-management evaluate its engagement strategies and make more
informed decisions about future events.

## Questions

**Question 1:** What percentage of individuals who attend
free community events become first-time financial
donors within 12 months of their initial event attendance?

**Question 2:** How is community event participation
associated with long-term financial support, particularly
repeat donations and donor retention?

## Analysis plan

### Question 1: Event Participation and Donor Conversion

To answer the first question, I will merge the event
participation and contribution datasets using their
shared Contact ID variable.

I will first clean the datasets by standardizing dates,
reviewing missing values, and filtering participation
records to include individuals marked as "Attended."
I will also exclude future events and identify which
events qualify as non-monetary community events.

Next, I will identify each individual's first recorded
event attendance and determine whether they had made
a financial contribution before attending. Individuals
who donated previously will be classified as existing
donors rather than new donors.

For individuals without prior donations, I will calculate
whether they made their first financial contribution
within 365 days of their initial attendance. I will
restrict this calculation to individuals with a complete
12-month follow-up period.

The main variables will include Contact ID, Event ID,
Event Title, Event Start Date, Participant Status,
Contribution ID, and Contribution Date.

New variables will include first attendance date,
first donation date, prior donor status, days between
attendance and donation, and conversion within
12 months (Yes/No).

I plan to create a bar chart showing the percentage
of eligible event attendees who became first-time
donors compared with those who did not. I may also
compare conversion rates across different years or
event categories.

### Question 2: Event Participation and Long-Term Support

To answer the second question, I will examine whether
individuals who participate in more community events
demonstrate different donation patterns than those
who attend fewer events.

Using the merged datasets, I will calculate the
number of events attended by each individual, the
number of completed contributions they made, and
their total donation amounts.

I will also identify donors who made multiple
contributions and examine whether they donated
again within 12 months of their first donation.
Comparisons will use consistent observation periods
where possible.

The main variables will include Contact ID, Event ID,
Event Start Date, Contribution ID, Contribution Date,
and Total Amount.

New variables will include total events attended,
total contributions, total donation amount, repeat
donor status (Yes/No), and donation retention
within 12 months (Yes/No).

I plan to use bar charts to compare repeat donation
rates across event participation groups and line
charts to visualize donation activity over time.

Because the data is observational, this analysis
will focus on identifying associations rather
than establishing that event participation
directly causes financial contributions.
